draft.title: Adaptations to Australian conditions
card: Much of Australia is hot and dry, with unreliable rain and regular bushfires. Many native species have adaptations that help them survive these conditions.
Some plants have deep roots that reach water far below the surface, or thick, waxy leaves that lose less water. Some animals shelter in burrows, where it is cooler and more humid than above ground.

Some eucalypts have thick bark that protects the tree, and buds under the bark that regrow new leaves after a fire. Some plants, such as many banksias, keep seeds in woody fruits that open after fire.
These features are inherited. Individuals with them were more likely to survive and reproduce in Australian conditions, so the features became common in the population.
draft.remember: Many Australian species have inherited features that suit heat, drought and fire.

a.q: Why is a burrow an adaptation to hot, dry conditions for a desert animal?
opts: It shelters the animal in cooler, more humid air
It lets the animal make its own water underground
It lets the animal bring its body heat up to the air's
It lets the animal avoid needing water at any time
a.why: The air in a burrow is cooler and more humid than the surface, so the animal loses less water and heat stress is lower. It does not remove the need for water, because the animal still has to drink or get water from food.
a.clue: Think about how the air underground differs from the air above.

b.q: After a bushfire in the Victorian bush, a eucalypt with blackened bark grows new leaves from its trunk. Which adaptation allows this?
opts: Buds protected under thick bark that regrow after fire
Deep roots that reach water far below the surface
Seeds held in woody fruits that open only after fire
Waxy leaves that lose less water in hot weather
b.why: New leaves growing from the trunk come from buds protected under the bark, so the same tree recovers. Seeds in woody fruits are also a fire adaptation, but they start new plants from seed rather than regrowing from the trunk.
b.clue: The new leaves grow from the tree that survived, not from seed.

a.best: It shelters the animal in cooler, more humid air

b.best: Buds protected under thick bark that regrow after fire

problems.detail: The distractor "It lets the animal bring its body heat up to the air's" is awkwardly phrased and hard to parse ("up to the air's" what?). Reword it, for example "It lets the animal warm its body to match the outside air".

The distractor "Seeds held in woody fruits that open only after fire" adds "only", but the card says the fruits "open after fire". This is a distractor, but the absolute is stricter than the card and not true of every banksia. Drop "only" to match the card.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, with one clearly right answer each. Minor fixes: an awkwardly worded distractor in (a), and an "only" in a distractor in (b) that the card does not state.
